expert_panel: Leber Congenital Amaurosis/early onset Retinal Dystrophy VCEP

aiva_evidence.PVS1: Met — Very Strong. Ensembl VEP annotates the GRCh37 deletion as p.Ala500SerfsTer11. ClinGen GN120 recognizes loss of function as a mechanism of recessive RPE65 retinopathy and explicitly assigns Very Strong to frameshifts from Ser2 through Gly528.
aiva_evidence.PS1: Not met — no distinct pathogenic or likely pathogenic comparator with the same protein change or qualifying splice effect was identified (GN120).
aiva_evidence.PS2: Not met — no de novo observation or parental testing was reported (GN120).
aiva_evidence.PS3: Not met — no qualifying functional assay of this deletion was identified, including an assay showing isomerohydrolase activity ≤10% of wild type (GN120).
aiva_evidence.PS4: Not applicable — GN120 excludes PS4 for RPE65.
aiva_evidence.PM1: Not applicable — this is a frameshift, not a missense substitution at a residue designated by GN120.
aiva_evidence.PM2: Met — Supporting. The successful Ensembl VEP lookup returned no gnomAD record for this genomic allele. This meets the specified absence rule; no numerical PopMax FAF was reported. GN120 uses a rarity cutoff of ≤0.0002.
aiva_evidence.PM3: Not met — no affected proband with a qualifying homozygous genotype or second RPE65 allele was documented. Recessive inheritance alone does not earn GN120 allelic points.
aiva_evidence.PM4: Not applicable — the five-base deletion shifts the reading frame; it is neither an in-frame indel nor a stop-loss variant (GN120).
aiva_evidence.PM5: Not applicable — GN120 requires a missense substitution; this allele causes a frameshift.
aiva_evidence.PM6: Not applicable — GN120 directs de novo evidence to PS2.
aiva_evidence.PP1: Not met — no segregation in a proband and a similarly affected relative, with evidence of two RPE65 variants in trans, was documented (GN120).
aiva_evidence.PP2: Not applicable — GN120 excludes PP2 for RPE65.
aiva_evidence.PP3: Not met — VEP SpliceAI maximum delta was 0.022, below the GN120 threshold of 0.2. The REVEL rule is for missense variants, not frameshifts.
aiva_evidence.PP4: Not met — the disease label and inheritance pattern do not document proband findings totaling the minimum four GN120 phenotype points.
aiva_evidence.BA1: Not met — no population frequency reaching the GN120 stand-alone cutoff of 0.008 was identified.
aiva_evidence.BS1: Not met — no population frequency within the GN120 BS1 range of 0.0008–0.008 was identified.
aiva_evidence.BS2: Not met — no report documented three well-phenotyped homozygotes unaffected by age 40, as required by GN120.
aiva_evidence.BS3: Not met — no qualifying assay demonstrated preserved function for this deletion, including isomerohydrolase activity ≥50% of wild type (GN120).
aiva_evidence.BS4: Not met — no similarly affected relative was documented to lack the relevant allele or genotype (GN120).
aiva_evidence.BP1: Not applicable — GN120 excludes BP1 for RPE65.
aiva_evidence.BP2: Not met — no pathogenic or likely pathogenic RPE65 variant was documented in cis with this deletion (GN120).
aiva_evidence.BP3: Not applicable — GN120 excludes BP3 for RPE65.
aiva_evidence.BP4: Not applicable — GN120 does not assign BP4 to a coding frameshift. The low SpliceAI score addresses splicing, not the altered reading frame.
aiva_evidence.BP5: Not applicable — GN120 excludes BP5 for RPE65.
aiva_evidence.BP7: Not met — this is a coding frameshift rather than a qualifying silent or intronic variant, and no qualifying RNA study was identified (GN120).

aiva_rationale: For the genomic allele GRCh37 1:68895558 ATAAGC>A, the evidence totals one Very Strong and one Supporting pathogenic criterion, with no benign criteria. ClinGen GN120 does not list that combination as Likely Pathogenic or Pathogenic; the score of 9 does not override its combining rules. VEP verified the genomic allele as ENST00000262340.5:c.1498_1502del but did not independently confirm the supplied NM_000329.3:c.1501_1505del description. The protein-level literature search found no indexed report; follow-up coding-name searches were rate-limited, so published case evidence could not be excluded.

disease: overgrowth syndrome and/or cerebral malformations due to abnormalities in MTOR pathway genes

aiva_evidence.PVS1: not_applicable — GN018 specifies gain of function, not loss of function, as the disease mechanism; p.Ile1216Val is missense.
aiva_evidence.PS1: not_met — No different nucleotide substitution producing p.Ile1216Val was established as pathogenic for this phenotype (GN018).
aiva_evidence.PS2: not_met — No parental testing or paired-tissue allele fractions were reported for this variant. The stated mosaic inheritance pattern does not establish either GN018 de novo criterion.
aiva_evidence.PS3: not_met — Literature searches identified no variant-specific assay demonstrating gain of function that meets GN018 validation requirements.
aiva_evidence.PS4: not_met — No variant-positive cases with scorable clinical findings were identified, and the GN018 PM2 prerequisite was not met.
aiva_evidence.PM1: not_met — The available domain annotations do not establish Ile1216 as a critical residue specified in GN018 Table 4.
aiva_evidence.PM2: not_met — VEP reports 4/108,548 alleles in gnomAD v2.1.1 exome controls. No ancestry-matched cohort establishing qualifying rarity was identified, and the gnomAD joint group-maximum frequency exceeds the GN018 BS1 threshold.
aiva_evidence.PM3: not_applicable — GN018 excludes this recessive allelic criterion for the heterozygous disorder.
aiva_evidence.PM4: not_applicable — GN018 excludes PM4; this substitution also leaves protein length unchanged.
aiva_evidence.PM5: not_met — No different missense change at Ile1216 was verified as pathogenic for this phenotype (GN018).
aiva_evidence.PM6: not_applicable — GN018 evaluates de novo and tissue-mosaic evidence under PS2 rather than PM6.
aiva_evidence.PP1: not_applicable — GN018 excludes cosegregation for this de novo or mosaic disorder.
aiva_evidence.PP2: met — Supporting: p.Ile1216Val is missense, and MTOR has a missense Z-score of 10.32 per the gnomAD constraint lookup, above the GN018 threshold of 3.09.
aiva_evidence.PP3: not_applicable — GN018 excludes missense pathogenicity predictors for this gain-of-function mechanism.
aiva_evidence.PP4: not_applicable — GN018 evaluates qualifying phenotype details under PS4, not as independent PP4 evidence.
aiva_evidence.BA1: not_met — The gnomAD v4.1 joint group-maximum AF is 0.08221% per VEP, below the GN018 stand-alone threshold of >0.0926%. The higher dbNSFP value is from All of Us, not gnomAD.
aiva_evidence.BS1: met — Strong: VEP reports a gnomAD v4.1 joint group-maximum AF of 5/6,082 (0.08221%), above the GN018 disease-specific threshold of >0.0185%.
aiva_evidence.BS2: not_met — VEP reports zero gnomAD v4.1 homozygotes, and there is no documentation of the three well-phenotyped unaffected heterozygous relatives required by the alternative GN018 rule.
aiva_evidence.BS3: not_met — No variant-specific assay demonstrating normal function and meeting GN018 validation requirements was identified.
aiva_evidence.BS4: not_applicable — GN018 excludes nonsegregation evidence for this de novo or mosaic disorder.
aiva_evidence.BP1: not_applicable — GN018 excludes BP1 because truncating loss-of-function variants are not the established mechanism for this phenotype.
aiva_evidence.BP2: not_met — No known pathogenic MTOR variant was documented in cis or in trans with p.Ile1216Val (GN018).
aiva_evidence.BP3: not_applicable — GN018 excludes BP3; this variant is also not an in-frame indel.
aiva_evidence.BP4: not_applicable — GN018 restricts BP4 to specified synonymous, intronic or UTR variants. Neither REVEL nor a low SpliceAI score qualifies this missense variant.
aiva_evidence.BP5: not_met — No affected carrier with an established alternate molecular diagnosis was identified (GN018).
aiva_evidence.BP7: not_applicable — This missense substitution is outside the synonymous, intronic and UTR classes eligible under GN018.

aiva_rationale: MTOR NM_004958.3:c.3646A>G (p.Ile1216Val) meets one Strong benign criterion (BS1) and one Supporting pathogenic criterion (PP2). Its gnomAD group-maximum frequency falls between the panel’s BS1 and BA1 thresholds. PP2 reflects gene-level constraint, not evidence that this allele activates MTOR. Under the requested combining rules, one BS without a BP is insufficient for Likely Benign, and one PP is insufficient for Likely Pathogenic. The result is therefore VUS (leaning benign) for the stated phenotype, independent of the ClinVar label.

aiva_rationale: For the verified genomic allele, PVS1 (Very Strong) plus PM2 (Supporting) gives 9 points. GN120 does not list one Very Strong plus one Supporting criterion as a Likely Pathogenic combination, so the classification remains VUS (leaning pathogenic). The variant-specific literature lookup found no indexed paper; the follow-up search by coding notation was rate-limited. Before clinical reporting, reconcile the identifiers: VEP annotated the genomic allele as ENST00000262340.5:c.1457_1458del, and equivalence to the supplied NM_000329.3:c.1459_1460del was not verified. This classification should not be transferred to the RefSeq description without that check.

aiva_evidence.PM5: not_met (GN120): No different His527 substitution classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic under GN120 was verified.
aiva_evidence.PM6: not_applicable: GN120 evaluates de novo evidence under PS2 rather than PM6.

aiva_evidence.PP2: not_applicable: GN120 does not use gene-level missense constraint as PP2 evidence for RPE65.
aiva_evidence.PP3: met — Moderate (GN120): VEP reports REVEL 0.991 for p.His527Arg, exceeding the RPE65 Moderate cutoff of 0.774. This is a protein-effect prediction, not a splice prediction.
aiva_evidence.PP4: not_met (GN120): PMID:35904185 reports two RPE65 variants, nyctalopia, severely depressed full-field ERG responses and absent peripheral fundus autofluorescence. aiva_evidence.BP3: not_applicable: GN120 excludes BP3 for RPE65.

aiva_evidence.BP5: not_applicable: GN120 excludes BP5 for RPE65-related retinal dystrophy.
aiva_evidence.BP7: not_met (GN120): This is a missense substitution, not a synonymous or intronic change eligible on splice prediction alone; no qualifying RNA assay was identified.

aiva_rationale: RPE65 NM_000329.3:c.1580A>G (p.His527Arg) meets the GN120 Likely Pathogenic rule for autosomal recessive RPE65-related retinopathy: two Moderate criteria (PM1, PP3) plus two Supporting criteria (PS3, PM2), with no benign criteria. The direct functional finding is loss of detectable activity in a panel-approved assay. No Strong or Very Strong criterion was established, and the retrieved evidence does not meet a GN120 Pathogenic combination.

aiva_rationale: For NM_000329.3:c.1451G>T (p.Gly484Val) in autosomal recessive RPE65-related retinopathy, the independently verified evidence yields one Moderate and two Supporting pathogenic criteria, with no benign criteria. This combination does not meet a GN120 Likely Pathogenic rule: with one Moderate criterion and no Strong criterion, four Supporting criteria are required. ClinVar lists an expert-panel Pathogenic classification, but that label was not counted as evidence. The key limitation is that the retrieved primary passages did not verify enough independent biallelic cases, segregation, or scored clinical features to reproduce that classification.

aiva_rationale: RPE65 NM_000329.3:c.1292A>G (p.Tyr431Cys) meets the GN120 Likely Pathogenic rule for autosomal recessive RPE65-related retinopathy: two Moderate criteria (PM3, PP3) plus two Supporting criteria (PM2, PP4), with no benign criteria met. The evidence does not reach a Pathogenic combination, and the existing ClinVar label was not counted.

aiva_rationale: For autosomal dominant alpha-actinopathy, ClinGen GN147 gives Likely Pathogenic with one Strong and at least two Supporting pathogenic criteria. The variant-specific knock-in mouse provides Strong evidence; population rarity, missense constraint, and REVEL provide three Supporting criteria. The single benign Supporting criterion concerns splicing alone and does not reach a benign combination. The verified evidence does not reach a Pathogenic combination, and the existing ClinVar label was not counted.

aiva_rationale: For MSH6 NM_000179.3:c.1282A>G (p.Lys428Glu) and autosomal dominant Lynch syndrome, PP3 at Moderate was the only criterion met (score +2). aiva_rationale: For DYSF-related autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, rarity and the missense prediction contribute one Supporting point each. The total of 2 falls in the GN180 uncertain-significance range of 0–5, below the 6 points required for Likely Pathogenic. The published sibship is relevant, but the partner allele’s classification and a second affected segregation were not established from the retrieved evidence. The existing ClinVar assertion was not counted as evidence; this assessment is limited by incomplete verification of the case and functional data.

aiva_rationale: For autosomal recessive Usher syndrome, one benign Supporting criterion (BS1) and one pathogenic Supporting criterion (PP3) yield a score of 0. Neither side meets a Likely Benign or Likely Pathogenic combining rule. The required directional label leans benign because the population evidence is directly observed, whereas the evidence for damage is predictive. The published homozygous case does not resolve the conflict because it carries a second homozygous MYO7A change.

aiva_rationale: TECTA NM_005422.2:c.487-7C>G is Benign for autosomal dominant nonsyndromic deafness. Its Middle Eastern gnomAD frequency exceeds the GN005 stand-alone benign threshold in both exomes and genomes. One stand-alone benign criterion and one strong benign criterion met their thresholds; both reflect the same population evidence, and BA1 alone determines the class. No pathogenic criterion was met. The exact-variant literature search found no indexed passage, and the alternate-notation follow-up was rate-limited.

aiva_rationale: VWF c.3940G>C (p.Val1314Leu) was reported de novo in a patient with type 2B von Willebrand disease. Under the requested generic rules, one Moderate criterion (PM6) plus two Supporting criteria (PM2, PP2) yields 4 points and does not meet a Likely Pathogenic combination. No benign criteria were met. The ClinVar classification was not counted as independent evidence.

aiva_rationale: The HGVS-defined deletion is Likely Pathogenic as an allele for autosomal recessive PAH deficiency. Under the ACMG/ClinGen constitutional CNV technical standard (Riggs et al., 2020, Table 1, copy-number loss), the GRCh37 interval chr12:103245031–103249845 is 4,815 bp and affects one protein-coding gene, PAH. ClinGen rates PAH HI 30 (recessive disease, not established dominant haploinsufficiency) and TS 0 (no evidence). Scoring: §1A = 0; §2E = +0.90 for one Very Strong PVS1; §3A = 0 for one gene; §4 = 0 for lack of qualifying independent case or population evidence; §5F = 0 because transmission is unknown. The total of 0.90 reaches Likely Pathogenic (0.90–0.98), not Pathogenic (≥0.99). The integer score of 8 summarizes PVS1 strength, not CNV points. This allele alone does not establish a biallelic diagnosis. Before clinical reporting, reconcile the breakpoint notation: VEP anchors the HGVS deletion at chr12:103245030 with retained A, whereas the supplied VCF-style fields retain G at 103245031. They predict the same coding loss but do not specify identical genomic breakpoints.

aiva_rationale: Likely Pathogenic as an allele for autosomal recessive PAH-related phenylketonuria. The governing standard is the ACMG/ClinGen constitutional CNV technical standard (Riggs et al., 2020), copy-number loss rubric. VEP maps the 1,671-bp deletion to GRCh37 chr12:103260148–103261818 after normalization. It affects one protein-coding gene, PAH. ClinGen rates PAH haploinsufficiency 30 (recessive disease, not established dominant haploinsufficiency) and triplosensitivity 0 (no evidence). Scoring: §1A, coding content, 0; §2E, intragenic frameshifting exon loss meeting PVS1, +0.90; §3A, one gene, 0; §4, no independently scorable case or population evidence, 0; §5F, transmission unknown, 0. The total of 0.90 meets Likely Pathogenic (0.90–0.98), but not Pathogenic (≥0.99). The integer acmg_score of 8 summarizes one Very Strong criterion; it is not the CNV score. This allele classification does not establish a molecular diagnosis without evidence that both PAH copies are affected.

aiva_rationale: Likely Pathogenic as an allele for autosomal recessive PAH-related phenylketonuria. Ensembl VEP maps the 5,354-bp deletion to GRCh37 chr12:103259491–103264844 inclusive, affecting one protein-coding gene, PAH. Under the ACMG/ClinGen constitutional CNV technical standard (Riggs et al., 2020, Table 1, copy-number loss), section 1A scores 0 for coding content; section 2E scores +0.90 for an intragenic deletion producing an early frameshift (PVS1 Very Strong); and section 3A scores 0 for one gene. No qualifying independent section 4 evidence was identified, and inheritance of this particular allele is unknown (5F, 0). The CNV total of 0.90 meets Likely Pathogenic (0.90–0.98), not Pathogenic (≥0.99). The separate integer acmg_score of 8 summarizes one Very Strong criterion; it does not determine the CNV class. ClinGen rates PAH HI 30 (autosomal recessive phenotype, not established dominant haploinsufficiency) and TS 0 (no evidence for triplosensitivity). Zygosity and a second allele in trans were not documented, so the deletion alone does not establish a biallelic molecular diagnosis.

aiva_rationale: For autosomal recessive PAH-related phenylketonuria, p.Arg169Cys meets one Moderate criterion (PM5) and two Supporting criteria (PM2, PP3), with no benign criteria. This combination does not meet a Likely Pathogenic rule in GN006 v2.1: one Moderate criterion requires at least four Supporting criteria. The variant has been observed in affected cohorts, but the retrieved evidence does not establish a qualifying biallelic genotype or measured loss of enzyme activity. The classification is therefore uncertain, leaning pathogenic, independent of ClinVar's label for Arg169Cys itself.

aiva_rationale: For autosomal recessive PAH-related phenylketonuria, the exact allele is rare and is predicted to weaken the splice donor. These findings provide two Supporting pathogenic criteria, with no Moderate, Strong, Very Strong, or benign criteria. Two Supporting criteria alone do not meet a GN006 v2.1 Likely Pathogenic rule. aiva_rationale: For autosomal dominant HNF1A monogenic diabetes, three pathogenic Supporting criteria and no benign criteria were met. GN017 has no Likely Pathogenic combination consisting solely of three Supporting criteria. The domain location, population absence and REVEL prediction therefore favor pathogenicity but do not establish it. VEP reports a ClinVar expert-panel Likely Pathogenic assertion for this allele; the retrieved evidence did not independently reproduce that classification, and the assertion itself was not counted.

Population rarity contributes one Supporting pathogenic criterion (PM2, +1). The net score of −5 falls in the GN009 Likely Benign range of −6 to −2; Benign requires −7 or lower. The existing ClinVar label was not used as evidence.

aiva_rationale: For TP53 c.1025G>C (p.Arg342Pro) and Li-Fraumeni syndrome, one Supporting pathogenic criterion and no benign criteria were independently verified. This evidence-limited assessment differs from the expert-panel Pathogenic record in ClinVar (215996); it is not evidence that the panel classification is wrong. The published carrier and functional observations favor pathogenicity, but the retrieved evidence did not establish the case-level points or assay combination needed to score them under GN009.

aiva_rationale: For autosomal recessive Pompe disease, allele-specific RNA evidence and a molecularly phased affected case support pathogenicity. Using the returned GN010 strengths gives 3 Moderate criteria and 1 Supporting criterion, meeting the ACMG/AMP Likely Pathogenic rule of ≥3 Moderate. Using PM2 at Supporting as specified in the full GN010 narrative instead gives 2 Moderate and 2 Supporting, also Likely Pathogenic. Neither combination reaches Pathogenic, and no benign criterion was met.

aiva_rationale: This classification applies only to GRCh37 chr19:1398999 CGG>C. VEP maps that two-base deletion to ENST00000447102.3:c.484_485del (p.Pro162GlyfsTer28). aiva_rationale: The classification applies only to the GRCh37 POS/REF/ALT allele. VEP maps it to ENST00000359596.3:c.13014_13033del (p.Ala4339ArgfsTer237). The variant-indexed literature lookup was rate-limited; a separate search by coding and protein notation found no matching publication.

aiva_rationale: For autosomal dominant malignant hyperthermia susceptibility, the verified evidence comprises one Moderate pathogenic criterion (PP3) and no benign criteria. That combination does not reach Likely Pathogenic. The exact G>C allele was reported in an MH event, but that case alone falls below the panel's PS4 threshold. The key unresolved issue is allele identity: because G>C and G>T both encode p.Val4234Leu, protein-only reports cannot establish additional cases or segregations for G>C. This assessment is limited to the evidence verified here; the existing ClinVar label was not counted.

aiva_rationale: For autosomal dominant HNF4A monogenic diabetes, the verified evidence totals one Moderate criterion and two Supporting criteria, with no benign criteria. This combination does not meet a GN085 v4.0 Likely Pathogenic rule. ClinVar records an expert-panel Pathogenic assertion for this allele, but the accessible evidence did not independently establish qualifying case counts, segregation, or functional results. The VUS classification reflects that evidence limitation, not evidence against pathogenicity.

aiva_rationale: GN085 v4.0 yields one Moderate criterion (PM1), two Supporting criteria (PM2 and PP3), and no benign criteria. VEP reports an expert-panel Pathogenic assertion in ClinVar, but the assertion itself was not counted, and the retrieved passages did not establish additional qualifying case, segregation, or functional evidence.

aiva_rationale: This classification is for the genomic allele only. The two submitted identifiers describe different deletions: GRCh37 20:43047063 AGG>A deletes GG at 43047064–43047065, whereas NM_175914.5:c.583-2del deletes A at 43047063 (VCF 20:43047062 CA>C). No enumerated GN085 combining rule matches that combination, yielding VUS under the requested rule precedence. GN085's PVS1 and PM2 comments explicitly call this same combination Likely Pathogenic; the difference is in the combining instructions, not in the evidence. Neither the published pedigree nor the ClinVar assertion for the single-base deletion was counted.

aiva_rationale: For autosomal dominant HNF4A monogenic diabetes, GN085 yields one Strong and one Supporting pathogenic criterion, with no benign criteria (score 5). This combination falls short of Likely Pathogenic: one Strong requires at least one Moderate or two Supporting criteria. The distinction is exon-specific: loss of the native donor is strongly predicted, but exon 5 skipping preserves the reading frame, so the panel assigns PVS1_Strong rather than PVS1_VeryStrong. The literature searches were unsuccessful, leaving variant-specific RNA, case and segregation evidence unverified rather than shown to be absent.

aiva_rationale: This classification applies only to GRCh37 X:18646815 TAT>T. The two identifiers describe different alleles: the genomic record deletes AT at X:18646816–18646817, whereas VEP maps NM_001323289.2:c.2821del to deletion of a single T at X:18646815 (VCF X:18646814 CT>C). Evidence for the single-base deletion was not transferred. For the two-base deletion, one pathogenic Supporting criterion (PM2) and no benign criteria meet no GN034 pathogenic or benign combination. Rarity alone does not establish causality. Confirm the intended allele against the original laboratory record and obtain its consequence on the major brain transcript before using this result clinically.

SpliceAI predicts loss of the native donor and possible use of a donor 46 nucleotides downstream, which would shift the reading frame. Biallelic loss of function causes recessive Noonan syndrome (PMID:39258154). Very Strong was withheld because the actual splice product and extent of residual normal transcript were not established.

aiva_rationale: For autosomal recessive LZTR1-related Noonan syndrome, 1 Strong + 1 Moderate + 2 Supporting criteria meet the GN094 Likely Pathogenic rule of 1 Strong + 1 Moderate. That rule is satisfied by the predicted loss-of-function allele and the phased recessive case alone, without relying on the splice prediction twice. The available evidence does not reach a GN094 Pathogenic combination. This is an allele classification, not a recessive diagnosis from a single allele.

aiva_rationale: For the GRCh37 genomic allele X:135067657 GAG>G, one pathogenic Supporting criterion (PM2) and one benign Supporting criterion (BP4) yield a score of 0. Neither side reaches a GN033 classification threshold. The evidence is balanced; the required “leaning benign” label does not establish a benign effect. Variant identity matters here: the genomic allele deletes two bases (AG), whereas NM_001379110.1:c.-57+21del as written denotes a single-base deletion. Confirm the transcript HGVS before applying this classification to a clinical report; it applies only to the two-base genomic deletion.

This supports Strong rather than Very Strong loss-of-function evidence under the GN027/Tayoun framework.

aiva_rationale: For MECP2 NM_001110792.2:c.1469G>A (p.Arg490Gln) and Rett syndrome, the ClinGen lookup returned no VCEP specification, so the requested generic rules were used. No pathogenic or benign criterion met a threshold at any strength (score 0). The allele is present in population data, but rarity alone supports neither direction here, and REVEL falls between the benign and pathogenic cutoffs. No combining rule fired. ‘VUS (leaning benign)’ is the requested label for this zero-criterion result, not a conclusion that benignity has been demonstrated. The ClinVar label was not counted as evidence.
